atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence in 1903 from our dossiers, one for every eligible event in the year table, placed on 1910 county lines and month by month through the year. Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro: Encyclopedia-style accounts of 590 episodes of anti-Black violence in 1903, written from both the Black press (Dangerous Press) and the white press (Chronicling America). They come from 911 dossiers on events drawn at random, in seeded draws, from our 1903 event table, until the whole table had been drawn; when a drawn event already had a dossier from one of our other 1903 runs, that dossier was used. Two more cover events first found as leads inside other dossiers. Thirty-eight more drawn events were recognized before any work as duplicates of episodes already covered and were merged instead, and from the later draws sixty-two were set aside from the table entry alone, without a dossier, as plainly out of scope (twenty-seven routine arrests, twelve manhunts or forecasts with no one hurt, seven with no race given, seven objections or strikes with no force, six with Black attackers or no racial motive, three white victims). Of the 911 dossiers, 321 were set aside: eighty-nine shootings or beatings in routine arrests, escapes or custody; fifty-nine manhunts, chases, sieges, rumors or quarrels in which no Black person was hurt (including manhunts where a lynching was only “feared” or talked of, with no threat made and no crowd formed); thirty-six where no report gives the victim’s race; thirty-six with no racial motive or with Black attackers; twenty-eight objections, boycotts, strikes or taunts against Black people with no force or threat; nineteen duplicates of other entries; nineteen whose victims were white or other; nineteen two-sided fights; eight that took place in another year (1870 to 1902, reprinted or recalled in 1903); seven that a contemporary source disputes, that no located article supports, or that come from fiction; and a legal execution. Each entry gives the type the papers support. A research agent found and judged the coverage; a second agent read it and wrote the account; code checked every citation and quotation. At most ten clippings per entry, the fewest that back every statement; Black-press clippings are page images, white-press ones the article text. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
